newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK DEVELOPMENT MIN DENIES TALKS ON PRIVATE TELECOMS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK DEVELOPMENT MIN DENIES TALKS ON PRIVATE TELECOMS.

text.p: Greek Devepolment Minister Vasso Papandreou did not discuss the setting up of a private telecoms firm with prominent businessmen on Thursday as reported in the press on Friday, the ministry said in a statement.
Greek daily Kathimerini reported today that the government was seeking to set up a private telecoms company.
"The government is seeking the participation of the biggest groups of Greek companies in a new telecommunications organisation that will operate as a second OTE," it said.
The sole purpose of the meeting was to coordinate the activities of state and private companies in the Balkans and Eastern Europe, the ministry said.
Greek Development Minister, Vasso Papandreou met with businessmen Vardis Vardinoyannis, Socrates Kokkalis, Nikos Grigoriadis of the Latsis Group and Dionysis Kopelouzos on Thursday.
The top management of Public Petroleum Corporation (DEP) and Public Power Corporation (DEH) were also present at the meeting. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
